title: The Three Factions
objective: Meet the powers in Crestfall. Find Maret.

text.default:
The soldier on the gate is young and holds himself rather too straight, like a man who has been given authority recently and is still getting used to it. Through the gate behind him two more soldiers are doing nothing, very efficiently.

He introduces himself as Lieutenant Cael. It is a city name, and a career soldier's. He smiles with the lower half of his face.

"We have been expecting somebody to arrive asking questions, [sir/ma'am]," he says. "The town always gets one sooner or later. Somebody from outside who cares about what is happening here." He waits a moment, but not long enough for you to answer. "The Compact cares about what is happening here. We have been here eight months. We would like to help."
text.commander:
He stands up straighter when he sees the way you stand, before he knows who you are. A soldier knows rank even when he is trying to be diplomatic.

"Lieutenant," you say, and leave it at that.

"Commander," he says. So he has made enquiries.
text.arcane: He has been told to look out for scholars and mages coming in from outside. You see him decide that you are one, and you let him. So the Compact has people who know what to look for. That is interesting, and not altogether comfortable.
text.ranger:
Cael sees you coming across the market square and puts himself in your way, quite naturally, so that it does not look as if he meant to. He has done it before.

"Just arrived?" he asks, though he knows perfectly well.

"Yesterday," you say.

"So we heard."
text.cipher:
He is good at this, though not very good. You saw him change his approach twice between first seeing you and your reaching the gate. The smile has been practised, and so has the friendliness.

He said somebody, you notice, and not you. He is waiting to see whether you will correct him.

choices.text: "What does the Compact want?"

default.text:
He tells you plainly, which you had not expected. The Compact wants the ruins to the east looked over: how far they go, how safe they are, what is in them. They think the curse comes from there, and that whoever controls the source controls the cure. Or the weapon, you think. He doesn't say weapon, but he leaves a space for it.

In return there is money, protection, and the use of Compact supplies in the region. He takes out a sealed packet, a message for somebody on the east road. "Just deliver it," he says. "Think of it as an introduction to the way we work."

choices.text: Ask his commission date, and who signed it.

default.text:
He tells you the date, the regiment and the colonel's name. Somewhere in the telling the smile goes, and what is left is a young officer who has been sent somewhere difficult and is not at all sure he was expected to come back.

"Sir," he says, and starts to correct himself, and doesn't finish.

choices.text: "What does the Compact know about what's happening here?"

success.text: Cael tells you more than he means to. Under the official phrases about a coordinated response and protecting the region, you can make out what the Compact really thinks. Their scholars have spent eight months trying to put a name to what is in those ruins and have failed. And they have come to believe the curse is not a disease at all, but a signal.

success_at_cost.text: Cael gives you the official line, and gives it well. You can't tell whether there is more underneath or whether that is all there is. Either way, you would need to talk to somebody more senior than a lieutenant.

failure.text: He gives you the official line from start to finish, and you take it without pressing him. It is smoother than it ought to be, as if it has been said a good many times before, but that is all you get.

text.default:
Cael sets out the terms clearly. The Compact wants somebody in the ruins. They have soldiers, but soldiers are noticed; they put people's backs up. What they want is somebody who comes and goes on their own account and belongs to no side, and just now that is worth more to them.

In return they will give you fifteen coins now and forty when the work is done. You would have the use of the Compact's supplies, food and medicine and equipment, which in Crestfall is no small thing. And if anything goes wrong that one person can't handle, the Compact will send people.

"We are not your enemies," Cael says. "And we are not pretending to be your friends. We are a business arrangement, if you want one."
text.commander:
He puts the offer plainly, and you think the better of him for it. The Compact wants information from the ruins and will pay for it.

You have worked with outfits like the Compact before. They are reliable right up to the moment their interests part company with yours. You notice that they want the ruins looked over, and that nobody has said they want the curse stopped.
text.arcane:
The offer makes sense, and it is obvious enough what lies behind it. The Compact thinks there is something in the ruins it wants, and wants you to tell it what.

What interests you more is what he leaves out. The Compact has already had scholars at the edge of the ruins, and they came back calling what they found older than the Compact, older than the kingdom, older than any record anybody has.
text.ranger:
It is a practical offer: money, supplies, and somebody to come for you if it goes badly. The Compact's business needn't be yours for the arrangement to be useful, so long as you know what they are after and allow for it.

What you don't like is the sealed message. You make a point of never carrying a message without knowing what is in it.
text.cipher: It is a clean offer from a man who knows how to make one. The Compact is organised, which is more than can be said for anyone else in this town. But being organised has its drawbacks. Organisations do what their leaders decide, whether it is right or not.

choices.text: Accept the offer.

default.text:
Cael nods once, as a man does when something has gone as he expected. He hands you the packet and the first fifteen coins, and gives you a name on the east road: a woman called Sera, who keeps what looks like a waystation and isn't.

"Don't open the packet," he says. "She'll know if you have." He says it quite flatly, and you can't tell whether it is a threat or a test.

choices.text: Refuse. You aren't working for anybody.

default.text:
"Understood," says Cael. The smile does not move. "The offer stays open. We are not going anywhere." He steps aside from the gate.

You can feel him watching you for some way down the street.

choices.text: Make a counter-offer. You want to see the message before you carry it.

success.text:
Cael considers you. Then he breaks the seal himself and hands you the packet.

The message turns out to be dull, a requisition for supplies and a request for more men. There is nothing sinister in it. You hand it back.

"Fair," he says, and seems to mean it. He offers you thirty coins now and thirty when the work is done, which is a little better than before. You have bargained with him, and he respects that.

success_at_cost.text: Cael won't open the message, but he offers you a better rate, twenty coins now, and tells you the contents are only logistics. You take the money without seeing the contents. You are better off than you were, but you are no less uneasy.

failure.text:
"The packet stays sealed," Cael says, still smiling. "That's the arrangement, or there isn't one."

He waits. It is the same offer as before.

text.default:
The shrine is in the old alderman's hall. You remember it with a different flag over the door and a different sort of authority inside. The Ashen Covenant's flag is grey, which may mean something, or may only be the colour they happened to choose.

Edric is outside when you get there, as though he knew you were coming, which very likely he did. In a town of this size news of a stranger gets about very quickly.

He is a composed man in his fifties, who found his answers a long time ago and is quite settled in them, though he is not smug about it.

"You arrived last night," he says, simply to let you know that he knows.
text.commander:
Edric looks you over as a man does who has been trained to read people. It is not a soldier's way of looking. He is trying to make out what sort of soul you are, and where to put you.

"A soldier," he says, which is right. "And something more than a soldier now." That is right too, in the way that vague remarks generally are.
text.arcane:
Edric looks at you, and you look at him, and for a moment you each understand that the other knows rather more about your own line of work than is comfortable.

He has ritual knowledge, and old knowledge at that; the Covenant's texts go back further than most of the kingdom's history. He has been near the curse long enough for his resistance to it to show on him, like the green on an old roof.

"A scholar," he says. "Or a mage. In practice the Covenant does not distinguish."
text.ranger:
Edric watches you cross the square with the patience of a man who has watched people come to him for thirty years. He reads the way you walk, and you read the way he stands still.

"A hunter," he says, which is fair. "From outside Ashenveld." That is fair too. He puts his head a little on one side. "People from outside always look at the forest differently. They know it less, and trust their noses more."
text.cipher:
Edric knew you were coming before you arrived, and manages to look as if he did not, which takes skill. His calm is practised rather than natural. If you know where to look you can see the effort in it.

"A traveller," he says. It is quite true, and tells you almost nothing. He is doing exactly what you are doing, and that interests you at once.

choices.text: "What does the Covenant believe is causing this?"

success.text:
He gives you the doctrine. The Covenant believes the curse came of the ruins being disturbed: an old power, sealed long ago, has come unsealed, and the people of the region had already drifted away from the old ways that kept it shut. Punishment is too simple a word for what he means. He means a consequence, the natural result of meddling with what had been left alone for good reason.

But under the doctrine you catch something else. He has been in those texts thirty years, and he knows the ritual that sealed the power the first time, and exactly what it required. When he talks about the cure he does not sound like a man of faith. He sounds like a man who has done the sums.

success_at_cost.text: He gives you the doctrine. It hangs together well enough, provided you accept a number of ideas about the world that you may or may not share. The curse is a consequence, the cure is purification, and the Covenant knows how it is done.

failure.text: He gives you the doctrine, and you take it as you find it. It is a belief, and you have met beliefs before. This one goes into more detail than most.

choices.text: "I'm going east. What should I know?"

default.text:
His face does not change, but he becomes noticeably more attentive.

"Do not go east," he says. "Not yet. Not without preparation, and not without knowing what you are walking towards. People who go east unprepared come back changed, or they do not come back at all. The Covenant has ways of preparing people. I would offer them to you."

text.default:
Inside, Edric shows you the ward they have put round the building. You cannot see it, but he explains: herbs laid along the threshold, stones set in certain patterns, and a chant the priests keep up in shifts of three hours. It has kept the worst of the curse away from the shrine and the people in it.

"The forest holds something that ought to be held," he says. "A power that was sealed away by the people who lived here before history began. The seal wore thin, and three years ago it failed."

He looks at you. "The Covenant knows how to seal it again. We have the texts, and we know the ritual."

Then he goes on. "But the ritual requires that the source be purified. Everything the power has touched, and touched deeply, must be cleansed. Completely."

He lets the word cleansed stand, and does not explain it.
text.commander:
"Purified," you say. "How?"

He tells you, quite calmly, in the voice doctors use for procedures that will hurt. He keeps what is necessary and what it costs carefully apart.

You keep your face still. So this is what the Covenant calls a cure.
text.arcane:
You listen carefully to the words he uses. Purified, cleansed. They are the words of an order that has a technical meaning for them, and uses them so as not to say what they mean in practice.

"What does cleansing involve?" you ask.
text.ranger:
"Who decides what's been touched deeply enough to need cleansing?" you ask.

He takes longer over the question than the answer seems to need. "The Covenant sets the threshold," he says at last. "From the texts. It is not arbitrary."

He has told you how it is decided. He has not told you who decides.
text.cipher:
You leave the word where he put it and watch his face while he watches yours.

He believes it, and that is what matters. He isn't cynical, and he isn't hiding something monstrous behind a pleasant manner. He honestly believes the ritual is necessary, and that the cost is simply the cost.

That makes him more dangerous than a man who knew he was doing harm.

choices.text: "What does cleansing mean, exactly?"

success.text:
He tells you. The ritual requires that everything badly afflicted by the power, whether people or animals or places, be separated from the world. He says released. You hear killed.

Not all of them, he is careful to add. The threshold is serious exposure. The early stages, the stillness and the dimming, may well be reversible, and the Covenant believes it can tell the one from the other.

You believe that they believe it.

success_at_cost.text: He gives you the words for it: separation, release, a loss that has to be borne for the good of the whole. What that would mean for the people you have already met in the town, he does not say.

failure.text: He gives you the doctrine without the details, and you do not press him. Just how far the Covenant means to go is something you will have to find out somewhere else.

choices.text: Trace the ward's pattern with a finger, without touching it.

default.text:
You hold your finger a hair's breadth above the carving and follow the lines. It is not a shield at all. The lines run in a grid, square on square, with a mark at every crossing, like a surveyor's plan. Whoever wears this is not being protected. They are being used to take measurements.

Edric watches you do it and says nothing.

choices.text: "What isn't the Covenant telling the town?"
choices.locked_hint: Needs the Covenant to trust you

default.text:
He takes his time. "That we have done this before," he says. "Not here. In the south, two hundred years ago. The texts say it worked."

He does not say what it cost. He looks as if he expects you to ask, and is relieved when you don't.

choices.text: Ask about the preparation they offer for those going east.

default.text:
He gives you a ward: a small stone disc with markings on it, threaded on a cord. He hands it over carefully, as one hands over something of real value.

"It will not protect you from everything," he says. "But it will slow the effect of long exposure. Keep it next to your skin." He asks for nothing in return. You gather the Covenant works on credit. They help you, and you are left knowing that they helped you.

default: Before you go, Edric takes out a small carved stone and holds it out to you.

"There is a place on the east road where the tree line turns at a sharp angle," he says. "Our scholars believe it is a nexus, where the channels of the curse come together near the surface. If you are going east in any case, it would be a service to us if you placed this marker there."
It may slow the spread of the curse along that road, he says. He says it as though he were giving you the odds on a horse.
"It may do nothing," he admits. "We cannot be certain. We act on probabilities."
"A senior scholar is coming from the capital," he adds. "Seriva. She will want to know the stone was placed."
text.commander:
You take the stone. It is a plain enough job, with a clear place to do it. You will put it down if it is on your way, and that does not make you a servant of the Covenant.

Edric seems to understand the difference.
text.arcane:
The markings on the stone come from a tradition older than the Covenant. You have seen notation like it in texts written centuries before the present church existed. Somebody in the Covenant has access to writings most scholars believe were destroyed long ago.

You take the stone, and you say nothing about recognising the marks.
text.ranger:
You look the stone over before you take it. The carving is regular and careful, the work of somebody who knew what they were making, though you don't know the mark.

You take it. If the place is where Edric says, you will pass it anyway.
text.cipher:
You take the stone. Now you owe the Covenant a favour, and how large a favour depends on how useful the stone turns out to be. If it does nothing, the debt is small. If it works, you will owe them a good deal.

Edric is buying goodwill cheaply. You rather admire the way he does it.

choices.text: Take the marker stone, and place it if you pass that way.

default.text:
You take the stone and Edric nods. He has not asked very much of you, and he has gained one more pair of hands.

"Travel safely," he says, and he means it.

choices.text: Decline. You aren't running errands.

default.text:
"Of course," says Edric, perfectly composed. He was not relying on you. He puts the stone away; there are other people he can ask.

"The ward is still yours," he says. "There are no conditions."
By midday you have some idea of the three powers in what is left of Crestfall.
default.else: By midday you have met one of the powers in what is left of Crestfall and heard about the others.

default.text: The Compact wants the ruins. They are organised, they have money, and they are patient. For eight months they have been working towards something.
default.else: The Compact holds the gate. People say they want the ruins and are patient about it.

default.text: The Covenant wants the ruins sealed, and believes it knows how. What that would cost is something they prefer not to mention first.
default.else: The Covenant has the old hall and a grey flag. People say they know how to seal the curse, and do not say what it costs.

default: The Rootless live outside the town and nobody talks about them, which makes them the most interesting of the three.

Three different people have now given you Maret's name. None of them quite recommended her and none of them quite warned you off. They said her name as people talk about the weather coming in, as something you would have to deal with whether you liked it or not.
text.commander:
You have spent half a day with two of the three powers. You know what each of them wants, and you have formed a first opinion of each.

The Compact is useful, and needs watching. The Covenant is not your friend, may well be your enemy, and certainly knows things. The Rootless you know nothing about, which is the most dangerous position to be in and much the most interesting.
text.arcane:
You have seen two of the three. Each knows part of the truth, and neither has all of it.

The Rootless have been living beside the curse for three years, longer than anyone else in Ashenveld. Whatever they know, they have learned the hard way.
text.ranger:
You have seen two of the three. The third lives outside the town's control and has been surviving next to the curse for three years.

People who have survived in bad country are the ones worth listening to. You are going to the camp.
text.cipher:
Two sides, two offers, and you know roughly what each is after. The third is the one nobody claims as a friend and nobody openly opposes. When there are three parties to a quarrel, the one in the middle generally has the most say.

Maret is the one in the middle.

choices.text: Go to the Rootless camp east of the town.

default.text: You go east out of the market, past the last house, along something that is not quite a path, and in among the first of the trees, where the town stops and the forest has not yet taken over.

choices.text: Go back to the Tallow first, and ask Aldous about the camp.

default.text:
Aldous is wiping the same table as last night. "The camp," he says, and thinks about it. "Take bread. Don't take advice. And don't stand in the path, the big one doesn't like it."

He gives you the bread.

text.default:
There are fifteen tents, and a fire in the middle burning even at midday. Along the south side runs a herb garden that is doing far better than it has any right to in this soil at this time of year.

A man steps out from between two of the tents as you arrive. He is big and in no hurry, like a man who decided long ago that there is very seldom any need to move quickly.

"The camp is not open to visitors," he says. He is not unfriendly about it, only clear.

"I'm looking for Maret," you say.

He looks you over as though checking you against a list he keeps in his head. "Most people who come looking for Maret want something from her. What is it you want?"
text.commander:
The man is called Branch, you learn later, and he was a soldier once. It shows in the way he stands, and in the way he has put himself between you and the camp without seeming to.

You answer him as directly as he asked. "I'm looking for somebody who came through here about fourteen months ago. I was told Maret would know."

He looks at you as one old soldier looks at another. "Perhaps she does. That is hers to tell, not mine."
text.arcane:
The herb garden behind him has plants in it you know from the medical texts. They grow near places where power has collected, and they draw it off and dull it. Somebody here knows very well what they are doing with them.

"I'm a scholar," you say, which is partly true. "I'm trying to understand what's happening in this country."

He makes a sound that might be a laugh. "Everyone who comes to Maret is trying to understand something. She decides whether you should."
text.ranger:
He gives himself away before he has your measure. His shoulders are set, he has half turned towards the camp as if guarding it, and he has the calm of a man who has been in danger often enough to stop being surprised by it.

"You came by the north path," he says. "Not the main way."

"It's shorter," you say.

He considers that. "Careful, or experienced. Maret likes both."
text.cipher:
You have Branch's measure at once. He has been a soldier, and he is loyal to Maret rather than to the Rootless in general. He is careful because he was trained to be, not because it is his nature.

"I'm not here to take anything," you say. "I'm here to ask questions."

"Everyone says that," he says. "Some of them are even telling the truth."

choices.text: "Someone I'm looking for came through here. I only need to know where they went."

success.text:
He looks at you, and makes up his mind.

"Wait here," he says, and goes back into the camp. A few minutes later a woman comes out.

Maret is not what you expected, though you could not say what you did expect. She is about your own age, and weathered, as people are who have lived out of doors for years and stopped minding. She looks straight at you, as she very likely looks at everything, and does not put on any manner for your benefit.

"Branch says you are looking for someone," she says.

success_at_cost.text: He considers you. "Half the people who turn up here say that." He looks at your pack and at the way you stand, working something out. "Maret will see you. But do not push her. She will give you what she wants to give you." He goes to fetch her.

failure.text:
"Maret is busy," he says. He is not unfriendly yet, but he is not going to budge either. "Come back tomorrow."

The day is nearly over. You will have to try the camp again tomorrow, and try it differently.

choices.text: "I can help. Whatever the camp needs, I can turn my hand to it."

success.text:
He looks at you with more interest. He is not convinced, but in a camp that is short of everything, somebody offering instead of asking is a change.

"What can you do?" he asks. And then he goes to fetch Maret.

success_at_cost.text: He is not won over, but he does not dismiss the offer either. He goes to fetch Maret without promising anything, and you wait.

failure.text: "Maret has enough people who can turn their hand to things," Branch says. He doesn't send you away, but he doesn't go to fetch her either. You will get no further today.

text.default:
You sleep at the Tallow and walk back out at first light.

Branch is standing between the same two tents, as if he had never moved. He watches you come up the path. He doesn't look surprised. He looks like a man who has had to change his opinion of somebody and is not altogether pleased about it.

"You came back," he says. "Most do not."

choices.text: Say nothing. Sit down on the stump by the path and wait.

default.text:
You sit down. He goes back to watching the trees. The camp wakes up behind him. After the best part of an hour a woman comes out from between the tents, looks at you, looks at Branch, and says, "How long has that one been sitting there?"

"Long enough," says Branch.

choices.text: "I'm not selling anything. I'm looking for [missing person]."

default.text:
The name does what yesterday's words did not. He looks at you differently.

"Wait here," he says.

default: She comes out of the camp and looks at you, and for a second something shows in her face before she puts it away. She knows the name you are going to say. You have not said it yet, but she knows.
That is the first thing you learn about Maret.

default.text: Three people have given you her name, and none of them said it lightly.

default: "Sit down," she says, and nods at a log bench on the edge of the camp. "I will hear what you have to say."

She sits down opposite you. Branch stands a little way off; somebody has asked him to. The camp goes on with its business around you. People come and go, a child is calling somewhere, and something is cooking.
"You are looking for someone," Maret says.
text.commander: She takes in the way you stand like a woman who has had dealings with commanders before and has done with taking their orders. She is not rude about it. She simply makes the terms clear.
text.arcane:
She looks at you as though she were reading more than your face, and you do the same to her. The residue on her is complicated, and lies in layers that would take some time to make out. She has been near the curse a long while, and it has not touched her. Whatever she did to keep it off, it was not the Covenant's method.

You give her the name. She knew it before you said it.
text.ranger:
Neither of you minds the silence. You are both used to it, and you both know what it is good for.

"You are not from Ashenveld any more," she says. "But you know the ground. You know where to put your feet."
text.cipher:
You have her measure in the first few seconds. She is controlled and clever, and used to deciding things on too little to go on, and by now she is good at it.

When you say the name, her hands, clasped in her lap, tighten for half a second. She covers it at once, and you pretend not to have noticed, and both of you know that you did.

choices.text: "You knew that name before I said it."

bonus.label: Corvin told you she sent them east

success.text:
She looks at you, and then does something you did not expect. She very nearly smiles.

"You notice things," she says. "That is useful here." She is quiet for a moment. "Yes. I knew them. They were here three weeks." She gives you the fact plainly, and nothing that goes with it, not yet.

"Where did they go?"

She looks at the trees. "East," she says, as though she had still not made up her mind how she felt about it.

success_at_cost.text: She sees that you have caught her, and decides quickly what to do about it. She neither denies it nor quite admits it. "I meet a great many people who come through the camp," she says. "Some names stay with me." Then: "Come back tomorrow. I need to think about what I can tell you."

failure.text: She turns it aside without any trouble. "A great many people come through the camp. I try to help the ones I can." Her voice is quite steady. "Come back tomorrow. I have things to see to today."

choices.text: Say the name, and watch her hands, not her face.

default.text:
You say the name. Her face does nothing at all. Her hands, in her lap, take hold of each other and do not let go.

"You knew," you say.

She looks at her hands, and then at you, and doesn't pretend.

choices.text: Don't push yet. Ask about the camp and her people first.

default.text:
She warms a little at this, though not much. The wariness she met you with eases by a degree.

She tells you about the camp. There are people from the villages to the east, people the town didn't know what to do with, people whose families stopped wanting them once the curse had touched them. There are twenty-three of them at present, and she runs it on practical lines.

"Why do you do it?" you ask.

She thinks about it longer than the question seems to need. "Because somebody has to," she says. "And I am here."
